P0100.title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Malfunction
P0100.detail: The MAF sensor signal is out of range or missing. Usual causes are a dirty or failed MAF sensor, a loose intake duct, or a wiring fault. Drivable but expect rough idle and poor fuel trim; get it checked soon.

P0101.title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Range/Performance
P0101.detail: The MAF reading doesn't match other engine data. Often a dirty sensor element, a vacuum/intake leak, or a clogged air filter. Safe to drive short term, but fuel economy and power will suffer until fixed.

P0102.title: Mass Air Flow Circuit Low Input
P0102.detail: MAF signal is reading lower than expected. Typically a failing sensor, a disconnected connector, or wiring damage. Address soon; the engine may run rich or hesitate.

P0103.title: Mass Air Flow Circuit High Input
P0103.detail: MAF signal is reading higher than expected. Usually a sensor fault or an electrical short in the wiring. Can cause a lean condition; get it looked at soon.

P0106.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Barometric Pressure Circuit Range/Performance
P0106.detail: The MAP sensor reading doesn't track engine load correctly. Common causes are a vacuum leak, clogged vacuum line, or a failing MAP sensor. Fine for now, but fix soon to avoid rough running.

P0107.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Circuit Low Input
P0107.detail: MAP sensor voltage is too low. Usually a bad sensor, damaged wiring, or a disconnected vacuum hose. Can cause poor idle and stalling; address soon.

P0108.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Circuit High Input
P0108.detail: MAP sensor voltage is too high. Often a failed sensor or a short to voltage in the harness. Address soon; may cause rich running and reduced power.

P0111.title: Intake Air Temperature Circuit Range/Performance
P0111.detail: The IAT sensor reading is implausible. Usually a corroded connector or a failing sensor. Minor drivability impact; not urgent but worth fixing for accurate fuel trim.

P0112.title: Intake Air Temperature Circuit Low Input
P0112.detail: IAT sensor signal reads too low (short to ground or failed sensor). Low urgency; can cause slightly rich running in cold starts.

P0113.title: Intake Air Temperature Circuit High Input
P0113.detail: IAT sensor signal reads too high (open circuit or failed sensor). Low urgency; may affect cold-start fueling slightly.

P0116.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Circuit Range/Performance
P0116.detail: Coolant temp reading is implausible given engine conditions. Could be a failing sensor or genuine cooling issue. Worth checking soon since it affects fueling and can mask overheating.

P0117.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Circuit Low Input
P0117.detail: Coolant temp sensor reads too low (short to ground or failed sensor). Can cause the ECU to run rich thinking the engine is cold. Address soon.

P0118.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Circuit High Input
P0118.detail: Coolant temp sensor reads too high (open circuit or failed sensor). Can mask a real overheat condition since the gauge may read wrong; get it checked soon.

P0121.title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0121.detail: TPS signal doesn't match expected throttle movement. Usually a worn or failing throttle position sensor. Can cause hesitation or surging; address soon.

P0122.title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit Low Input
P0122.detail: TPS voltage reads too low. Often a bad sensor or wiring fault. Can cause reduced power or limp mode; address soon.

P0123.title: Throttle Position Sensor Circuit High Input
P0123.detail: TPS voltage reads too high. Often a bad sensor or short in wiring. Can cause surging or limp mode; address soon.

P0125.title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control
P0125.detail: The engine is taking too long to reach operating temperature, or the sensor is faulty. Usually a stuck-open thermostat or bad coolant temp sensor. Not urgent but hurts fuel economy and emissions.

P0128.title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature
P0128.detail: Engine is running cooler than the thermostat should allow. Almost always a stuck-open or failing thermostat. Not dangerous, but fix soon since it hurts fuel economy and heater output.

P0130.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0130.detail: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is invalid. Usually sensor failure, wiring damage, or an exhaust leak near the sensor. Affects fuel trim and emissions; fix soon.

P0131.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0131.detail: Upstream O2 sensor voltage stuck low, suggesting a lean condition or failed sensor. Common causes: vacuum leak, exhaust leak, or worn sensor. Address soon to protect the catalytic converter.

P0132.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0132.detail: Upstream O2 sensor voltage stuck high, suggesting a rich condition or failed sensor. Common causes: leaking injector, high fuel pressure, or worn sensor. Address soon.

P0133.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0133.detail: The upstream O2 sensor is reacting too slowly to switch rich/lean. Usually sensor aging or contamination. Not urgent but hurts fuel economy and emissions over time.

P0134.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0134.detail: The upstream O2 sensor isn't switching at all, possibly a dead sensor, open circuit, or exhaust leak. Fix soon; the engine may be running an open-loop guess at fuel mixture.

P0135.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0135.detail: The heater element in the upstream O2 sensor has failed or lost power. Usually a bad heater circuit or blown fuse. Not an emergency, but the sensor won't work correctly until fixed.

P0136.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0136.detail: The downstream (post-catalyst) oxygen sensor signal is invalid. Usually sensor failure or wiring damage. Low urgency; mainly affects catalyst monitoring.

P0141.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0141.detail: The downstream O2 sensor's heater has failed. Usually a bad heater element or blown fuse. Not urgent, cosmetic to emissions monitoring.

P0150.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0150.detail: Same as P0130 but on the engine's other cylinder bank (V-engines). Usually sensor failure or an exhaust leak. Address soon for fuel trim and emissions.

P0151.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0151.detail: Bank 2 upstream O2 sensor stuck lean. Common causes: vacuum leak on that bank, exhaust leak, or worn sensor. Address soon.

P0152.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0152.detail: Bank 2 upstream O2 sensor stuck rich. Common causes: leaking injector on that bank or worn sensor. Address soon.

P0155.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0155.detail: Heater element failure on the Bank 2 upstream O2 sensor. Usually a bad heater or blown fuse. Not urgent.

P0161.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0161.detail: Heater failure on the Bank 2 downstream O2 sensor. Low urgency; mainly affects catalyst monitoring accuracy.

P0171.title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P0171.detail: The engine is getting more air or less fuel than expected on Bank 1. Common causes: vacuum leak, dirty MAF, weak fuel pump, or clogged injectors. Fine short-term but fix soon; prolonged lean running can damage the catalytic converter.

P0172.title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
P0172.detail: The engine is getting too much fuel or too little air on Bank 1. Common causes: leaking injector, bad fuel pressure regulator, or dirty MAF. Fix soon; wastes fuel and can foul spark plugs.

P0174.title: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
P0174.detail: Same as P0171 but on the engine's other cylinder bank. Common causes: vacuum leak or weak fuel delivery on that bank. Fix soon to protect the catalytic converter.

P0175.title: System Too Rich (Bank 2)
P0175.detail: Same as P0172 but on Bank 2. Common causes: leaking injector or fuel pressure issue on that bank. Fix soon.

P0181.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0181.detail: Fuel temperature reading is implausible, usually a failing sensor. Low urgency, mainly affects fine fuel trim adjustments.

P0190.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0190.detail: Fuel rail pressure sensor signal is invalid. Can be a sensor fault or wiring issue. Address soon since accurate fuel pressure is important for engine performance.

P0200.title: Injector Circuit Malfunction
P0200.detail: A general fault in one or more fuel injector circuits. Usually a wiring fault, connector issue, or failed injector driver. Can cause misfires; address soon.

P0201.title: Injector Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 1)
P0201.detail: The cylinder 1 fuel injector circuit has an electrical fault. Usually a bad injector, connector, or wiring. Can cause a misfire on that cylinder; address soon.

P0202.title: Injector Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 2)
P0202.detail: Same as P0201 but for cylinder 2. Address soon to prevent misfire-related engine damage.

P0203.title: Injector Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 3)
P0203.detail: Same as P0201 but for cylinder 3. Address soon to prevent misfire-related engine damage.

P0204.title: Injector Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 4)
P0204.detail: Same as P0201 but for cylinder 4. Address soon to prevent misfire-related engine damage.

P0205.title: Injector Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 5)
P0205.detail: Same as P0201 but for cylinder 5. Address soon to prevent misfire-related engine damage.

P0206.title: Injector Circuit Malfunction (Cylinder 6)
P0206.detail: Same as P0201 but for cylinder 6. Address soon to prevent misfire-related engine damage.

P0217.title: Engine Overtemperature Condition
P0217.detail: The engine has detected an overheating condition. Stop driving as soon as it's safe and let the engine cool; continuing to drive risks serious engine damage. Check coolant level and cooling fan operation.

P0230.title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
P0230.detail: The fuel pump's primary control circuit has a fault, usually a relay, wiring, or pump failure. Can cause stalling or no-start; address soon.

P0300.title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
P0300.detail: The engine is misfiring across more than one cylinder. Common causes: worn spark plugs, bad ignition coils, vacuum leak, or fuel delivery issue. A flashing check-engine light with this code means stop driving immediately, since raw fuel can destroy the catalytic converter.

P0301.title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
P0301.detail: Cylinder 1 is misfiring. Usual causes are a worn spark plug, a failing ignition coil, or a fuel injector issue on that cylinder. Fine for short trips but fix soon; a flashing light means stop driving now.

P0302.title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
P0302.detail: Same as P0301 but for cylinder 2. Fix soon; a flashing check-engine light means stop driving immediately.

P0303.title: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected
P0303.detail: Same as P0301 but for cylinder 3. Fix soon; a flashing check-engine light means stop driving immediately.

P0304.title: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected
P0304.detail: Same as P0301 but for cylinder 4. Fix soon; a flashing check-engine light means stop driving immediately.

P0305.title: Cylinder 5 Misfire Detected
P0305.detail: Same as P0301 but for cylinder 5. Fix soon; a flashing check-engine light means stop driving immediately.

P0306.title: Cylinder 6 Misfire Detected
P0306.detail: Same as P0301 but for cylinder 6. Fix soon; a flashing check-engine light means stop driving immediately.

P0307.title: Cylinder 7 Misfire Detected
P0307.detail: Same as P0301 but for cylinder 7. Fix soon; a flashing check-engine light means stop driving immediately.

P0308.title: Cylinder 8 Misfire Detected
P0308.detail: Same as P0301 but for cylinder 8. Fix soon; a flashing check-engine light means stop driving immediately.

P0316.title: Engine Misfire Detected on Startup (First 1000 Revolutions)
P0316.detail: Misfire specifically during cold start. Common causes include worn plugs, weak battery/starter cranking speed, or a cold-start fueling issue. Not usually an emergency, but worth fixing.

P0325.title: Knock Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1)
P0325.detail: The knock sensor signal is invalid, often a failed sensor or wiring fault. The ECU may pull timing as a precaution, costing power. Address soon to restore full performance and protect against undetected knock.

P0326.title: Knock Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P0326.detail: Knock sensor signal is implausible. Common causes are a loose sensor, wiring issue, or engine mount noise interference. Address soon.

P0327.title: Knock Sensor Circuit Low Input (Bank 1)
P0327.detail: Knock sensor signal too low, usually wiring or sensor failure. Address soon so the ECU can properly protect against engine knock.

P0328.title: Knock Sensor Circuit High Input (Bank 1)
P0328.detail: Knock sensor signal too high, usually a wiring short or failed sensor. Address soon.

P0330.title: Knock Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2)
P0330.detail: Same as P0325 but for the engine's other cylinder bank. Address soon to protect against undetected knock and restore full power.

P0335.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0335.detail: The crank position sensor signal is invalid. Common causes: failed sensor, damaged wiring, or a broken reluctor wheel. Can cause stalling or no-start; get it checked promptly.

P0336.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0336.detail: Crank sensor signal is implausible during running. Can cause intermittent stalling; address promptly since it may leave you stranded.

P0339.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0339.detail: The crank position signal cuts out intermittently, usually a wiring or connector fault. Can cause random stalling; address promptly.

P0340.title: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0340.detail: The cam position sensor signal is invalid. Common causes: failed sensor, wiring damage, or timing chain/belt issues. Can cause hard starting or stalling; address soon.

P0341.title: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0341.detail: Cam position sensor signal is implausible. Can indicate sensor wear, wiring issues, or timing chain stretch. Address soon.

P0344.title: Camshaft Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0344.detail: Cam position signal cuts out intermittently, usually a wiring or connector fault. Can cause intermittent stalling; address soon.

P0350.title: Ignition Coil Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
P0350.detail: A general ignition coil circuit fault. Usually a failed coil, connector corrosion, or wiring damage. Can cause misfires; address soon.

P0351.title: Ignition Coil A Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
P0351.detail: Fault in the circuit for ignition coil A (often cylinder 1). Usually a failed coil or wiring issue. Address soon; can cause a misfire.

P0352.title: Ignition Coil B Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
P0352.detail: Same as P0351 but for coil B. Address soon; can cause a misfire.

P0353.title: Ignition Coil C Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
P0353.detail: Same as P0351 but for coil C. Address soon; can cause a misfire.

P0354.title: Ignition Coil D Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
P0354.detail: Same as P0351 but for coil D. Address soon; can cause a misfire.

P0400.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Malfunction
P0400.detail: The EGR system isn't flowing as expected. Common causes: carbon-clogged EGR valve or passages, or a failed EGR valve. Not an emergency, but fix soon; can cause rough idle and increased emissions.

P0401.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Insufficient Detected
P0401.detail: The EGR valve isn't flowing enough exhaust gas, almost always due to carbon buildup clogging the valve or passages. Not dangerous, but can cause pinging/knock under load; fix soon.

P0402.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Flow Excessive Detected
P0402.detail: Too much EGR flow, often a stuck-open EGR valve. Can cause rough idle or stalling at low speed; address soon.

P0404.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Circuit Range/Performance
P0404.detail: The EGR valve position doesn't match commanded position. Usually a sticking valve or wiring issue. Not urgent but affects emissions and idle quality.

P0405.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit Low
P0405.detail: EGR position sensor signal reads too low. Usually a sensor or wiring fault. Low urgency.

P0406.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Sensor A Circuit High
P0406.detail: EGR position sensor signal reads too high. Usually a sensor or wiring fault. Low urgency.

P0410.title: Secondary Air Injection System Malfunction
P0410.detail: The secondary air injection system (helps warm up the catalyst) has a fault, often a failed pump or valve. Not urgent; mainly affects cold-start emissions.

P0411.title: Secondary Air Injection System Incorrect Flow Detected
P0411.detail: Secondary air system flow is wrong, usually a failing pump, valve, or hose leak. Not urgent.

P0420.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0420.detail: The catalytic converter isn't cleaning exhaust as well as it should. Often the catalyst itself is aging or worn out, but can also be caused by an upstream misfire, O2 sensor fault, or exhaust leak. Not an emergency, but will likely fail an emissions test.

P0430.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P0430.detail: Same as P0420 but for the engine's other cylinder bank. Check for misfires or exhaust leaks on that bank before assuming the catalyst itself is bad.

P0440.title: Evaporative Emission System Malfunction
P0440.detail: A general fault in the EVAP system, which controls fuel vapor from the tank. Very often just a loose or cracked gas cap. Not dangerous; low urgency.

P0441.title: Evaporative Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
P0441.detail: The EVAP purge valve isn't flowing vapor correctly. Usually a stuck purge valve or clogged line. Low urgency.

P0442.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Small Leak)
P0442.detail: A small fuel vapor leak was detected in the EVAP system. Check the gas cap first, then hoses and the purge/vent valves. Not dangerous, low urgency.

P0446.title: Evaporative Emission System Vent Control Circuit Malfunction
P0446.detail: The EVAP vent valve circuit has a fault, often a stuck valve or wiring issue. Not dangerous, low urgency.

P0455.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Large Leak)
P0455.detail: A large fuel vapor leak was found in the EVAP system, most commonly a loose, missing, or damaged gas cap. Check and tighten or replace the cap first. Not dangerous, but will trigger emissions test failure.

P0456.title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detected (Very Small Leak)
P0456.detail: A very small EVAP leak was detected, often a hairline crack in a hose or the gas cap seal. Not dangerous, low urgency.

P0460.title: Fuel Level Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0460.detail: The fuel level sending unit signal is invalid. Usually a failing sender or wiring fault. Affects fuel gauge accuracy only; not a safety issue.

P0480.title: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit Malfunction
P0480.detail: The primary cooling fan circuit has a fault, often a bad relay, fuse, or fan motor. Can lead to overheating in traffic or hot weather; address promptly.

P0500.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
P0500.detail: The vehicle speed sensor signal is invalid or missing. Can affect speedometer, cruise control, and shift timing on automatics. Address soon.

P0501.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Range/Performance
P0501.detail: Vehicle speed sensor reading is implausible. Similar effects and urgency to P0500; address soon.

P0505.title: Idle Control System Malfunction
P0505.detail: The idle air control system isn't behaving as expected, causing rough, high, or low idle. Often a dirty throttle body or failing idle control valve. Not urgent but annoying to drive with.

P0506.title: Idle Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
P0506.detail: Idle speed is lower than commanded, risking stalling at idle. Often a dirty throttle body or vacuum leak. Address soon.

P0507.title: Idle Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
P0507.detail: Idle speed is higher than commanded. Often a vacuum leak or stuck-open idle air control valve. Address soon.

P0525.title: Cruise Control Servo Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0525.detail: The cruise control actuator signal is implausible. Usually a failing servo or wiring issue. Not a safety-critical code but affects cruise control operation.

P0560.title: System Voltage Malfunction
P0560.detail: The ECU is seeing an abnormal system voltage, often from a weak battery, failing alternator, or poor ground connection. Address soon to avoid a no-start or electrical gremlins.

P0562.title: System Voltage Low
P0562.detail: System voltage is too low, usually a weak battery, bad alternator, or corroded connections. Get the charging system tested soon to avoid being stranded.

P0563.title: System Voltage High
P0563.detail: System voltage is too high, usually an overcharging alternator or bad voltage regulator. Can damage the battery and electronics; address soon.

P0600.title: Serial Communication Link Malfunction
P0600.detail: A module on the vehicle's internal communication bus isn't responding correctly. Can be a wiring fault or a failing module. Get it scanned properly to find which module is at fault.

P0601.title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
P0601.detail: The ECU's internal memory failed a check, suggesting a fault in the control module itself. Often requires ECU reprogramming or replacement; have it diagnosed.

P0602.title: Control Module Programming Error
P0602.detail: The ECU's programming is incomplete or corrupted, usually from an interrupted reflash. Needs to be reprogrammed by a shop with the right equipment.

P0603.title: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
P0603.detail: The ECU lost its keep-alive memory, often from a battery disconnect or voltage drop. Usually harmless; the ECU will relearn over time, but if it recurs, check the battery and connections.

P0605.title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
P0605.detail: A fault in the ECU's internal ROM, indicating a hardware issue in the control module itself. Have it diagnosed; may need ECU replacement.

P0606.title: ECM/PCM Processor Fault
P0606.detail: The main engine control processor detected an internal fault. This is a control-module hardware issue; have it diagnosed, as it can affect overall engine management.

P0620.title: Generator Control Circuit Malfunction
P0620.detail: The alternator control circuit has a fault, often wiring or the alternator itself. Can lead to charging issues; address soon.

P0630.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible - ECM/PCM
P0630.detail: The VIN stored in the ECU doesn't match or is missing, usually after a control module replacement that wasn't fully programmed. Needs shop reprogramming; not a driving safety issue.

P0650.title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) Control Circuit Malfunction
P0650.detail: A fault in the check-engine light's own control circuit, often a bulb, wiring, or driver circuit issue. Not a drivability issue, but means the warning light itself may not work correctly.

P0700.title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
P0700.detail: The transmission control module has detected a fault and stored its own codes. Have the transmission separately scanned for the specific fault; don't ignore it, as some transmission faults can cause sudden loss of drive.

P0703.title: Brake Switch Input Malfunction
P0703.detail: The brake pedal switch signal used by the transmission/cruise control is invalid. Can affect torque converter lockup and cruise control operation. Address soon.

P0705.title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit Malfunction (PRNDL)
P0705.detail: The gear selector position sensor signal is invalid. Can cause incorrect gear detection or starting issues. Address soon.

P0706.title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0706.detail: Gear selector position reading is implausible. Similar effects to P0705; address soon.

P0710.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0710.detail: Transmission fluid temp sensor signal is invalid. Can cause the transmission to run in a conservative limp mode; address soon.

P0715.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0715.detail: Transmission input speed sensor signal is invalid. Can cause harsh or incorrect shifting; address soon.

P0720.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0720.detail: Transmission output speed sensor signal is invalid. Can affect speedometer and shift quality; address soon.

P0725.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Malfunction
P0725.detail: The transmission isn't receiving a valid engine speed signal. Can cause poor shift quality; address soon.

P0730.title: Incorrect Gear Ratio
P0730.detail: The transmission isn't achieving the commanded gear ratio, suggesting internal wear, low fluid, or a solenoid fault. Have the transmission inspected soon; can worsen into more serious damage.

P0731.title: Gear 1 Incorrect Ratio
P0731.detail: First gear isn't achieving its correct ratio, suggesting a clutch, band, or solenoid issue in that gear range. Have the transmission inspected soon.

P0732.title: Gear 2 Incorrect Ratio
P0732.detail: Same as P0731 but for second gear. Have the transmission inspected soon.

P0733.title: Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio
P0733.detail: Same as P0731 but for third gear. Have the transmission inspected soon.

P0734.title: Gear 4 Incorrect Ratio
P0734.detail: Same as P0731 but for fourth gear. Have the transmission inspected soon.

P0740.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Malfunction
P0740.detail: The torque converter lockup clutch circuit has a fault. Can cause poor fuel economy or shudder at cruising speed; address soon.

P0741.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance or Stuck Off
P0741.detail: The torque converter clutch isn't locking up when commanded. Common causes: solenoid failure, low fluid, or internal wear. Address soon; hurts fuel economy and can shorten transmission life.

P0743.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Electrical
P0743.detail: An electrical fault in the torque converter clutch circuit, often wiring or the solenoid itself. Address soon.

P0750.title: Shift Solenoid A Malfunction
P0750.detail: A fault in one of the transmission's shift solenoids, causing harsh, delayed, or missing shifts. Have the transmission inspected soon; low fluid level is a common contributing cause.

P0755.title: Shift Solenoid B Malfunction
P0755.detail: Same as P0750 but for a different shift solenoid. Have the transmission inspected soon.

P0760.title: Shift Solenoid C Malfunction
P0760.detail: Same as P0750 but for a different shift solenoid. Have the transmission inspected soon.

P1000.title: OBD System Readiness Test Not Complete
P1000.detail: The emissions monitors haven't finished running yet, usually right after a battery disconnect or code clear. Not a fault; just drive normally through a few trips and it will clear on its own.
